criteria.text: `public/js/figures/atlas.js` and `public/js/figures/testimony.js` exist, are importable under `node:test` with no `document` defined, and neither one touches `document` at import time (same side-effect-free rule `app.js` has today) — checked by extending the existing "app.js is importable outside a browser" test to the two new files.

The import-graph test's `jsFiles()`/`moduleSource()` walk the `figures/` subdirectory too, and its `expected` graph is: `format.js: []`, `state.js: []`, `api.js: []`, `layout.js: ['./format.js']`, `render.js: ['./format.js', './layout.js']`, `figures/atlas.js: ['./api.js', './format.js', './layout.js', './render.js', './state.js']`, `figures/testimony.js: ['./api.js', './format.js', './render.js', './state.js']`, `app.js: ['./figures/atlas.js', './figures/testimony.js']`. The acyclic-import test passes against this graph.

`import('../public/js/figures/atlas.js')` exposes `mount`, `createHandlers`, `layoutKey`, `docsQuery`, `scopeKeys`; `import('../public/js/state.js')` exposes `fromScope` and `debounce` alongside the existing scope-memo exports; neither `state.js` nor `figures/testimony.js` exposes `outlet`/`zoom`/`layoutCache`/`mask`/request-id helpers.

`test/atlas-request-reuse-acceptance.test.ts` and `test/unified-atlas-acceptance.test.ts` import `createHandlers`/`docsQuery`/`scopeKeys` from `../public/js/figures/atlas.js` and `fromScope`/`debounce` from `../public/js/state.js`; every assertion in both files that is not about `resetOutlet` (see #6) passes unchanged.

`figures/atlas.js`'s `createHandlers` accepts no `resetOutlet` action and its `control('person')` handler never references an outlet; the "only the person control releases the outlet in focus" assertion is replaced by an equivalent one against `figures/testimony.js`'s own local handler table: changing testimony's own person, days or source control releases testimony's own focused outlet.

Given the fixture's two seeded people, mounting the page with `?atlas.person=<A>&testimony.person=<B>` results in figure 1's graph request naming `<A>` and figure 2's sources/testimony requests naming `<B>` — the two figures show different people at once. Checked by driving each figure's `mount()` with a fake DOM and a spied `fetch`, asserting the two request URLs.
Given `?days=7` alone, both figures' first request carries `days=7`; given `?days=7&testimony.days=365`, figure 1's request carries `days=7` and figure 2's carries `days=365`.

Changing figure 2's own person, days or source control triggers a new figure-2 request and does not trigger a new figure-1 request, and vice versa — checked by spying `fetch` call counts per figure before and after each change.
`#stats` no longer exists inside `<header class="top">` in `design-5.html`; `#atlasStats` exists inside `#workspace`'s `.figure-title`.

The top-level `<section class="sentence">` no longer exists in `design-5.html`; `#workspace`'s `.figure-head` contains a `.sentence-line` with `#person`, `#days`, `#source`, `#sort`, `#limit`; `#testimony`'s `.figure-head` contains a `.sentence-line` with `#testimonyPerson`, `#testimonyDays`, `#testimonySource`.
`GET /api/people` is fetched exactly once during `boot()` regardless of how many figures mount — checked by spying the fetch/`api.loadPeople` call count.

`figures/testimony.js`'s strip repaint on resize is driven by a `ResizeObserver` scoped to `#strip`; `figures/atlas.js`'s resize handling no longer reads or writes `#strip`, `#testimonyList` or `#outletList`.

`design-5.html` still has no `<style>` block, no inline `style=` beyond a `--var` override, and loads only `./bundle.js` as its one module script (the existing markup-shape assertions, re-run against the new markup).
`pnpm build` is rerun and `public/bundle.js` committed; the bundle-freshness test passes.
`pnpm typecheck` passes (every new module and every new/changed function parameter carries the JSDoc types `tsc` needs under `allowJs`/`checkJs`).
`pnpm test` passes in full, including every currently-green suite this issue touches.

`CLAUDE.md`'s architecture description and the docs describe the front-end as one module per figure under `public/js/figures/`, `app.js` as a shell that mounts them and exports only `boot`, and `state.js` as holding only the shared scope memo and the two generic helpers — a fact a human reviewer confirms by reading, not a string a test greps for.

Note: this issue's front-end tests are new territory for `test/docs-drift.test.ts` (that suite is about the collector registry and `docs/sources.md`, unrelated here) — no existing test covers criterion 18, so it stays a criterion, phrased against the fact rather than a file or heading.
